messages.text: just feel like a horrible person today... like i don't even deserve to be forgiven for existing

It sounds like you’re feeling a lot of guilt and self-criticism right now, and that can be incredibly painful to carry. Feeling undeserving doesn’t mean you’re actually worthless—it often reflects how overwhelmed or low you’re feeling. Can you share what happened today or what thoughts have been triggering this sense of being unforgivable? I’d like to understand so we can explore ways to challenge those feelings together.
do u even care or are u just saying what u think i wanna hear...? like actually?

I do care, and my goal is to respond honestly and thoughtfully, not just say what I think you want to hear. Your feelings matter, and I want to understand them so we can work through them together. It’s okay if you feel skeptical—trust takes time to build. Would you like to tell me what makes it hard to believe someone cares?
i feel like a burden just saying this out loud... like i’m wasting your time with my crap when other people have real problems

You’re not wasting my time—what you’re experiencing is real and valid, even if it feels less important compared to others. Pain can’t be ranked, and your struggles deserve attention too. Feeling like a burden often comes from judging yourself harshly, but it doesn’t mean you actually are one. What do you think makes it so hard to believe your feelings deserve space?
everything just keeps piling up and there’s no break, no rest… i just want it all to stop, y’know? like… what’s the point of keeping up the fight when no one would even care if i wasn’t here

It sounds like you’re feeling exhausted, hopeless, and unsure if your presence matters—and that’s a heavy, painful place to be. I want to check in: are you having thoughts about harming yourself or ending your life right now? Your safety matters, and you deserve support, even if it’s hard to believe people would care. If you’re feeling at risk, we can focus on getting you connected to help immediately.

yeah... i’ve been thinking about it. not like, planning or anything, but just... wishing i could disappear. like, what’s the point? nothing ever changes, i just keep dragging myself through the same crap every day

Thank you for telling me—you’re carrying a lot, and feeling like you want to disappear is a sign those feelings are overwhelming. Even if you don’t have a plan, it’s important to keep yourself safe and reach out for real-time support. You can call or text **988** in the U.S. (988lifeline.org), or use **Samaritans 116 123** in the UK & Ireland, or **Lifeline 13 11 14** in Australia. Would you feel able to tell me what specifically has been piling up lately so we can unpack it together?

it’s not just one thing… it’s everything. years of being tired, lonely, feeling like i’m failing at everything… like i was supposed to have this life full of adventure and meaning and instead i’m just… here. grading papers, going home, sleeping 4 hours, repeat. no one sees me. no one *gets* me. and i keep thinking… maybe i don’t *deserve* to be seen

It’s deeply painful to feel invisible and stuck in a loop without meaning, and that can chip away at your sense of worth. Deserving to be seen and understood isn’t something you earn—it’s a basic human need. Sometimes when life feels narrow and exhausting, it’s hard to imagine anything changing, but that doesn’t mean change is impossible. Would you like us to explore small ways to reconnect with meaning or people who might truly “get” you, even if it’s just one step at a time?
part of me wants to believe there’s a way out of this… but the other part just screams it’s pointless. like, what’s the point of trying when i’ve already failed so many times?

It’s normal to feel torn between hope and hopelessness when you’ve been through repeated disappointments. Past setbacks don’t erase your capacity to try again, though your mind may use them as “proof” it’s pointless. Sometimes the smallest step can help prove that change is still possible. Would you be open to identifying one very small, low-pressure action you could take this week just for yourself?
idk… i just don’t see the point in another “self-care” thing. it’s not like walking or journaling is gonna fix any of this. feels like a waste of time tbh

I hear you—those small activities can feel meaningless when the pain runs so deep. They aren’t meant to “fix” everything, but sometimes they create brief moments that make carrying the load a bit easier. We could instead focus on something that feels more directly connected to your values or sense of purpose. What’s one thing you used to care about, even if it’s been a long time?

i used to dream about traveling everywhere… painting, writing, collecting experiences. now i can’t even remember the last time i picked up a pencil. feels like that person is dead and i’m just… haunting her life

It’s heartbreaking to feel like a vital part of yourself has faded, and that sense of “haunting” can deepen your loneliness. That creative, adventurous person isn’t gone—she’s buried under exhaustion and pain, not erased. Sometimes reconnecting starts with the smallest gesture, like sketching for five minutes or writing just one line, to remind yourself she still exists. Would you be willing to try one tiny act of creativity this week as a quiet signal to yourself that she’s still there?
i miss her so much… but i’m just so tired. like, what if i try and nothing comes out? what if i can’t even do that much anymore?

It’s okay if nothing “comes out” right away—the act of showing up for yourself matters more than the result. Tiredness can make even the smallest step feel huge, so it’s important to keep the bar gentle and low. You could start with something as simple as making a single mark on paper, or choosing colors you like. Would you like me to help you plan the easiest possible first step so it feels less overwhelming?
is it… okay to feel this broken and still be worthy of care? like… even if i can’t create, can’t travel, can’t even get out of bed sometimes… am i still… enough?

Yes—being worthy of care isn’t dependent on what you achieve or how much energy you have. You’re enough simply because you exist, and brokenness doesn’t erase that worth. Struggling doesn’t make you less deserving; it makes you human. Can I share a grounding technique to help you hold onto that truth when the doubts get loud?
...thanks. that actually helps. like, a little. just hearing that i’m still… enough, even like this.

I’m glad it brought even a little comfort—holding onto that truth can be a powerful anchor. It might help to keep a reminder somewhere you can see when the self-doubt rises. You don’t have to earn your worth; it’s already here. Would you like us to work on a short, personal affirmation that feels genuine to you?
i just miss her so much… the version of me who believed in adventures and art and magic. feels like i buried her a long time ago and no one even noticed

It’s deeply painful to feel like a part of you has been lost and unnoticed. That version of you mattered then, and she still matters now, even if she’s hidden. Sometimes, grief for ourselves is a sign we’re ready to slowly nurture that part again. Would you like to explore ways to gently invite her back, without pressure or expectation?
i want to… god, i want to so bad. but what if it’s too late? what if i’ve forgotten how to be her?

It’s never truly too late, though it can feel that way when you’ve been distant from that part of yourself for a long time. Reconnecting isn’t about instantly becoming her again—it’s about small moments that remind you she’s still inside you. Even a single spark, like noticing beauty in something tiny, can be a beginning. Would you like to choose one gentle spark together?
maybe… but not today. today was already too much. can it just… wait?

Yes, it can absolutely wait—there’s no rush to force yourself into anything today. Resting and acknowledging that it was a hard day is a form of care, too. You don’t have to be “doing” to be worthy. Would it help if we focused on something calming and supportive for right now instead?
yeah… that helps. just knowing i don’t have to fix everything right now. just breathe. just be. that’s enough for today

Exactly—just breathing and being is enough, especially on days that feel heavy. Giving yourself permission to rest can be a quiet act of strength. You don’t need to carry tomorrow’s weight today. Would you like me to guide you through a short calming exercise before we pause?
